clauses.text: Public key systems using RSA, ECC, Diffie-Hellman, and DSA algorithms are vulnerable to Shor's algorithm
Ensure that all Websites and Applications are "https" enabled with a valid SSL/TLS Certificate.
Enforce strict TLS configurations by specifying approved cipher suites, certificate chains, and session parameters, and prohibit the use of weak or deprecated algorithms.
NIST will deprecate quantum-vulnerable public-key cryptography after 2030 and disallow its use under NIST standards and guidelines after 2035.
Digital signature generation: Disallowed, except where specifically allowed by NIST protocol-specific guidance; verification: Legacy use.
After December 31, 2023, three-key TDEA is disallowed for encryption unless specifically allowed by other NIST guidance.
After December 31, 2023, the use of PKCS1-v 1_5 padding scheme is disallowed.

Signature generation and key agreement below 112 bits of security strength are disallowed (Disallowed for < 112 bits (RSA len(n) < 2048; ECDSA len(n) < 224; DSA (L,N) not (2048,224),(2048,256),(3072,256))).
NSA intends that all NSS will be quantum-resistant by 2035. Algorithms: AES-256, ML-KEM-1024, ML-DSA-87, SHA-384/512, LMS/XMSS.

clauses.id: Master Direction on IT Governance (2023), para 16 Cryptographic controls
clauses.note: Applies to REs other than commercial banks; repealed for commercial banks by the 2026 Directions.
clauses.text: The key length, algorithms, cipher suites and applicable protocols used in transmission channels, processing of data and authentication purpose shall be strong. REs shall adopt internationally accepted and published standards that are not deprecated/ demonstrated to be insecure/ vulnerable and the configurations involved in implementing such controls shall be compliant with extant laws and regulatory instructions.

The key length, algorithms, cipher suites and applicable protocols used in transmission channels, processing of data and authentication purpose shall be strong. The bank shall adopt internationally accepted and published standards that are not deprecated / demonstrated to be insecure / vulnerable, and the configurations involved in implementing such controls shall be compliant with extant laws and regulatory instructions.

clauses.id: Box Item 7: Cybersecurity and Quantum Computing
clauses.text: REs shall maintain an inventory of cryptographic assets, prioritizing critical assets for Post Quantum Cryptography (PQC) migration, and assess their IT infrastructure capabilities. ... REs shall enhance their crypto-agility to ensure a seamless transition to quantum-resistant solutions without disrupting their current IT systems.
Risk assessment (including post-quantum risks) of REs' IT environment shall be done on a periodic basis.
Use industry standard, strong encryption algorithms (eg: RSA, AES etc.) wherever encryption is implemented. ... the right methodologies for storing the encryption keys
REs shall renew their digital certificates used in IT systems well in time.
Strong transport encryption mechanism such as TLS (Transport Layer Security, also referred to as SSL) should be used.
